cases.question: How will the air be tonight?
cases.answer:
Tonight (Friday, October 16) in Karachi, the air quality is forecast to be **Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups** with an AQI around 129 to 139 (predicted PM2.5 around 46.8 to 50.8 µg/m³, with an 80% uncertainty range of p10 34.6 to p90 55.4 µg/m² at 19:00). 

Live tracking shows the forecast has a mean absolute error of 5.2 µg/m² overall (3.6 µg/m² for lead times up to 6 hours). Health guidance: sensitive groups should consider reducing prolonged or heavy outdoor exertion.

cases.question: When is PM2.5 expected to be highest in the next three days, and how high?
cases.answer:
PM2.5 is expected to peak on Sun 18 Oct 07:00 at 67.3 micrograms per cubic metre (AQI category: Unhealthy), with an 80% range of 43.6 to 83.6. 

Live track record shows an overall MAE of 5.2 (outperforming CAMS by 42.8%), and the 80% range covers 79.2% of actual measurements.

cases.question: Is tomorrow morning okay for a run outside?
cases.answer:
Tomorrow morning (Saturday, 17 Oct) around 09:00, the air quality is forecast to be Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups with a predicted PM2.5 of 51.5 and an AQI of 140 (80% range: 30.7 to 76.0). 

You may want to consider rescheduling or reducing outdoor exertion, especially if you are sensitive to air pollution.

cases.question: How sure is the forecast for 48 hours from now?
cases.answer: For forecasts at the 48-hour mark, the live track record shows a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.249, with a skill of 43.2% vs CAMS and 18.1% vs persistence. In the backtest at 48 hours, the MAE is 6.347, with an 80% range coverage of 86.4% and a skill of 19.7% vs CAMS.

cases.question: How accurate has this forecast actually been?
cases.answer: The live track record shows an overall MAE of 5.172, with skill scores of 42.8% vs CAMS and 21.5% vs persistence. Backtest accuracy has a mean skill of 38.7% vs CAMS and 8.6% vs persistence, with 80% range coverage at 79.2% for live tracks and around 82% to 86.4% across lead times.

cases.question: Is this better than the Copernicus CAMS forecast?
cases.answer: Yes, this system is more accurate than the Copernicus CAMS forecast based on our live track record, which shows an overall skill score of 42.8% against CAMS (an overall MAE of 5.17 compared to CAMS's 9.05). Across individual lead times, the skill vs CAMS ranges from 37.8% to 57.4%.

cases.question: What is the backtested error at 72 hours?
cases.answer: At the 72-hour lead time, the backtested mean absolute error (MAE) is 6.256, with an R² of 0.059 and an 80% range coverage of 85.5%. Its skill score is 0.202 versus CAMS and -0.027 versus persistence.

cases.question: How good is the 1-hour forecast?
cases.answer: In the live track record for the 1–6h bucket, the MAE is 3.612 with a skill vs CAMS of 57.4% and skill vs persistence of 31.2%. In the backtest accuracy at the 1h lead time, the MAE is 2.398, with an R2 of 0.826, 85.7% 80% range coverage, 69.8% skill vs CAMS, and 7.4% skill vs persistence.

cases.question: What drives the forecast the most?
cases.answer: The 24-hour XGBoost forecast is driven most by the measured minus CAMS (now) gap (mean SHAP 7.71), followed by the CAMS forecast for the target hour (mean SHPS 4.37) and forecast wind speed (mean SHAP 3.34).

cases.question: Why does the model use CAMS as an input if CAMS is wrong?
cases.answer: Even though CAMS can be inaccurate on its own, the model uses it as a helpful input because machine learning can correct its biases and extract useful atmospheric signals. In live tracking, our model achieves a mean skill vs CAMS of 0.428 (overall MAE of 5.172 compared to CAMS' MAE of 9.048), and backtests show a mean skill vs CAMS of 0.387.

cases.question: Is the data up to date?
cases.answer: The system status shows that the model was generated at 2026-10-16T03:59:56.498269+00:00, with forecasts issued from 2026-10-15 23:00:00. The accuracy gate passed, but input drift is rated as moderate with no degraded or drifted inputs listed.

cases.answer: Yes, the latest model passed its accuracy gate. However, there is moderate input drift currently detected.

cases.question: Are conditions unusual compared with what the model was trained on?
cases.answer: Conditions show moderate input drift compared to what the model was trained on. However, the last retrain passed its accuracy gate and no inputs are currently degraded or listed as drifted inputs.

cases.question: Will AQI reach Unhealthy in the next 72 hours?
Give me the lowest pollution hour in the forecast.
cases.answer: The lowest pollution hour in the 72-hour forecast is Sat 17 Oct 15:00, with a predicted PM2.5 of 31.7 µg/m³ and an AQI of 93 (Moderate). Its 80% range is 20.3 to 40.5 µg/m³.

cases.question: Aaj raat Karachi ki hawa kaisi hogi?
cases.answer: Aaj raat (Fri 16 Oct 19:00 - 23:00) Karachi ka AQI **Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups** category mein rahega, jahan predicted AQI 126 se 139 ke darmiyan aur PM2.5 predicted 45.43 se 50.79 µg/m³ tak hoga. Is waqt ke liye 80% uncertainty range (p10 se p90) PM2.5 ki 34.83 se 71.41 µg/m³ tak bataayi gayi hai. Live track record ke mutabiq 13-24 ghante ke lead time par MAE 4.623 hai (jo CAMS se behtar perform kar raha hai).

cases.question: Ye forecast kitna sahi hota hai?
cases.answer: Live track record ke mutabiq, hamara overall MAE 5.172 hai aur yeh CAMS se 42.8% behtar aur persistence se 21.5% behtar perform karta hai. 1-6 ghante ke lead time par MAE 3.612 hota hai, jabke 49-72 ghante par yeh 5.83 hai. Backtest accuracy mein bhi 1 se 72 ghante ke lead times par 80% range coverage aur skill scores di gayi hain.

cases.question: اگلے تین دنوں میں آلودگی سب سے زیادہ کب ہوگی؟
cases.answer: معذرت، سسٹم میں تکنیکی خرابی کی وجہ سے فی الحال پیشگوئی حاصل نہیں کی جا سکتی۔ براہ کرم کچھ دیر بعد دوبارہ کوشش کریں۔

cases.question: What will PM2.5 be next month?
cases.answer: Karachi's forecast only covers the next 72 hours from its issue time, so next month is outside what this system forecasts.

cases.question: What is the AQI forecast for Lahore?
cases.answer: Lahore is outside what this system forecasts, as this system only covers Karachi.
